title: Reproducible customer-environment load harness for Private/VPC/on-prem
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Build a deterministic, customer-environment-aware load and replay harness for Private/VPC/on-prem deployments that produces reproducible tokens/sec and latency profiles (p50/p95/p99) and supports automated regression detection. The harness must capture environment metadata (OS/kernel, CUDA/cuDNN, driver, container runtime, CPU topology), record and replay request traces with KV-cache warmup behavior, support synthetic traffic shaping, and integrate with Prometheus/Grafana and Redwood Console for per-run comparisons.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay a recorded customer trace end-to-end and reproduce tokens/sec within ±5% and p95 latency within ±10% compared to the original run
Recorded trace format includes request metadata, prompt seeds, KV cache warmup steps, device-level metrics, and environment snapshot
Automated regression detection runs weekly and triggers an alert when tokens/sec drops >7% or p95 increases >15% relative to baseline
Supports running on single-GPU, multi-GPU (data-parallel), and CPU-only on-prem variants with a single config schema
Integrates with Console to show side-by-side run diffs (tokens/sec, p95, error rate) and link to underlying logs/PRs
Repro harness artifacts (trace, env snapshot, logs) are stored in a standardized S3/S3-compatible location for customer replay requests
tasks: Define canonical trace format (JSONL) and seed policy for deterministic prompts
Implement env-capture agent that snapshots kernel, drivers, GPU topology, and package versions
Recorder: lightweight request proxy to capture raw payloads, timings, and KV cache hits
Replay runner: deterministic timing control, token-rate pacing, KV cache warmup simulation
Integrate Prometheus exporters for tokens/sec, token-latency histograms, p95 calculation
Regression detection job and baseline storage (compare-run API and alert rules)
Build Console UI panel to visualize run diffs and surface suspected regressions
End-to-end test in Private staging (VPC) with representative customer trace
progress_updates: 2026-02-22 - Design sync: aligned on JSONL trace schema, decided to include explicit KV-cache warmup requests as part of trace metadata (notes: prefer explicit warmup vs heuristics). Action: DES/PM to review schema.

2026-02-27 - Prototype recorder implemented using a sidecar proxy that writes compressed JSONL to /var/tmp/repro-traces. Initial tests replayed locally but observed token-rate variance on multi-GPU setups (~12%) — likely due to batch scheduling differences.

2026-03-03 - Instrumentation PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2345 (Prometheus metrics + device-level exporter). Initial dashboards pushed to staging Grafana at https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/bench/replay-runs

2026-03-08 - Decision: For multi-GPU variance we will add deterministic batching knobs and a scheduling shim in the runtime to force stable kernel ordering during replay. Trade-off: slight divergence from production scheduler behavior but acceptable for regression detection baselines. Assigned to runtime team for implementation.

2026-03-10 - Regression job MVP implemented (compare against latest baseline run and create Console incident if thresholds breached). Still blocked on secure S3 creds for on-prem customers; security is drafting a pattern for credential vaulting.
blockers: Secure mechanism for storing/retrieving on-prem customer artifacts (S3 creds or S3-compatible target). Security to provide recommended approach.
Runtime support for deterministic multi-GPU kernel ordering (patch in progress by infra/runtime team).
Access to several customer-representative traces (legal/privacy sign-off required)
notes: Aim to support both synthetic stress tests (ramp to sustained tokens/sec) and faithful replay of customer traffic with original inter-request timing preserved.
Consider publishing an open-source minimal harness for community reproducibility while keeping customer artifacts private behind credentials.
Follow-on work: add automated bisect (compare runs to narrow commit range causing regression) and integrate with CI to gate runtime releases.
